claims.statement: Every Linear webhook is HMAC-SHA256-verified against LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET with a constant-time compare before any processing; a missing or mismatching linear-signature header is rejected with 401.

AgentSessionEvent processing requires a Linear-Delivery header (a missing header is a 400 before any KV access) and dedupes redeliveries on the KV marker event:{deliveryId} with a 1-hour TTL; the payload's webhookId is deliberately not the dedupe key because it is the registered-webhook id and constant across deliveries. Only AgentSessionEvent payloads are acted on — other subscribed event types are acknowledged and skipped.

The webhook endpoint responds 200 immediately and runs handleAgentSessionEvent under executionCtx.waitUntil; a strict payload-shape gate (type, action, organizationId, appUserId, webhookId, agentSession.id) rejects malformed AgentSessionEvents with 400 before dedupe.

handleAgentSessionEvent routes by action and signal: stop/cancel (agentActivity.signal === "stop" or action stopped/cancelled) stops the mapped control-plane session and deletes the issue mapping only after a successful stop call; a prompted action with an existing issue→session mapping becomes a follow-up; everything else — including a prompted event with no mapping, which is a reply to a clarification elicitation — starts a new session whose resolution comment is the clarification reply and whose actor is the replier.

Runtime Linear API access uses OAuth2 client-credentials tokens minted from LINEAR_CLIENT_ID/LINEAR_CLIENT_SECRET (30-day app-actor tokens), verified by a viewer identity query that must match the webhook organizationId and the installed appUserId, cached in KV at oauth:client-credentials:{organizationId} with the token lifetime as the KV TTL; no refresh token is kept for runtime access, and persisting a verified token deletes the legacy oauth:token:{organizationId} record.

A cached client-credentials token counts as a hit only if it parses against the stored-token schema, carries the canonical scope set, has expires_at > issued_at with a 5-minute expiry skew, and matches the organizationId (and the expected appUserId); invalid or unreadable cache entries are treated as misses and trigger re-issuance, and a KV read or write failure never fails the request.

Each Linear GraphQL call carries a 15-second timeout; on HTTP 401 the client forces a token renewal and retries the rejected request exactly once before raising LinearAuthError (client_credentials_rejected), so rotating LINEAR_CLIENT_SECRET recovers on the next cache miss or 401 without reinstalling the app.
Client-credentials issuance is deduplicated per (organizationId, expectedAppUserId) with an in-flight promise map, so concurrent webhook and callback handlers share one token request.

GET /oauth/authorize redirects to Linear's authorize URL with actor=app and scope read,write,app:assignable,app:mentionable to install the agent; the OAuth callback exchanges the code, mints and verifies a runtime client-credentials token, and persists it before reporting success, so the installation is complete only when a later Worker invocation can load the credential from KV.

When client credentials cannot be issued or verified (LinearAuthError), the agent-session handler logs agent_session.no_oauth_token and aborts without creating a session, calling the control plane, or falling back to a legacy refresh token.

resolveSessionTarget resolves the session target via a five-stage ladder — project→target mapping, label-filtered team→target mapping, an explicit owner/repo in the trigger or clarification-reply comment, Linear's issueRepositorySuggestions API (accepting the top suggestion with confidence ≥ 0.7), and an LLM classifier — returning null (no session created) when classification is too uncertain.

matchExplicitRepo matches repository full names case-insensitively with boundary guards (a neighbor that extends the repository path, including runs of dots connecting to a path character, defeats the match), and returns null when zero or several repositories are named, leaving the ambiguity to the classifier.

The LLM classifier short-circuits before any model call when zero or one repositories are available; it requests clarification when no repo matched, confidence is low, or confidence is medium with alternatives, and classifier errors also produce a clarification rather than a session. The classification model comes from CLASSIFICATION_MODEL (default claude-haiku-4-5), whose id alone selects the Anthropic or OpenAI provider, and exactly the matching provider key must be bound.

Team and project repo mappings are operator-managed KV records (config:team-repos, config:project-repos) validated key by key on read, so one malformed entry costs only its own key and falls through to the next resolution stage; entries are environment-first unions, so a stored entry carrying both environmentId and repo keys keeps resolving to its environment.

Mapping entries may name a repository (owner/name) or a saved environment (environmentId); environment entries are validated against the live environment list and skipped — falling through to the next stage — when the environment is deleted or unfetchable, and the create-session request carries exactly one of repoOwner/repoName or environmentId.

For environment targets, integration settings, the enabled-repos allowlist check, and the callback context's repoFullName are governed by the environment's first (primary) repository, centralized in resolveTargetIntegration so future environment-level settings change exactly one function.

A resolved target outside the integration's enabledRepos allowlist produces an error activity naming the subject (repository, or environment and its primary repository) and no session is created; with no configured settings the defaults are permissive — all accessible repositories in scope, both model overrides allowed, tool progress on.

Repository and environment catalogs are read through a fail-open cache — in-memory 60 s → signed control-plane GET → KV last-known-good copy (KV TTL 300 s) → fallback empty list — where a malformed fresh response never overwrites the last-known-good copy; a total failure surfaces as no environments/repos, causing mapping stages to fall through and the classifier to ask for clarification.

Session model resolution applies the priority model:* issue label (when allowLabelModelOverride) > user KV preference (when allowUserPreferenceOverride) > repository/environment integration config > env.DEFAULT_MODEL, normalized through the shared model catalog; reasoning effort uses the user's preference when allowed and valid for the model, else the config's effort only when the model itself came from config/default, else the model's default effort.

Per-user model and reasoning preferences are admin/API-managed KV records under user_prefs:{userId} (not settable from a self-service Linear screen), and the triggering user's Linear profile supplies actorDisplayName/actorEmail for session attribution.

All Linear-sourced text in prompts — issue title, description, recent comments, the agent instruction, clarification replies, and Linear's promptContext — is escaped and wrapped in tagged <user_content> blocks with an explicit do-not-follow directive, including already-escaped marker variants; Linear's promptContext is preferred over assembling the prompt from issue fields, and integration issueSessionInstructions is appended verbatim.

handleNewSession creates the session via a sig1-signed POST to https://internal/sessions (target fields, title "{identifier}: {title}", model, reasoning effort, actor display/email) validated by createSessionResponseSchema, stores the issue→session mapping, attaches the View Session external URL and plan stages, then POSTs the prompt to https://internal/sessions/{id}/prompt with { content, source: "linear", callbackContext }; failures emit error activities with the HTTP status and control_plane.* logs.

The issue→session mapping is stored under issue:{issueId} with a 7-day TTL and schema-validated on read; it routes follow-ups to the existing session, lets stop/cancel kill the sandbox session, and rehydrates the stored target identity for follow-up integration lookups; expired or absent mappings mean the next agent request legitimately starts a new session.

handleFollowUp re-attaches a rebuilt callback context (callback context is message-scoped, not inherited by the control plane), optionally includes a 500-character summary of the session's latest token event, wraps follow-up text and the agent summary in isolated untrusted blocks, and reports the prompt result back to Linear as a thought (with session link) or an error activity, logging agent_session.followup either way.

The agent session's Linear plan is a five-step checklist (Analyze issue, Resolve repository, Create coding session, Code changes, Open PR) driven through makePlan stages start/repo_resolved/session_created during dispatch and completed/failed at completion.

The control plane signs each callback with the destination bot's per-service SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET over the JSON of the payload without the signature field (original key order); the worker requires its own secret (500 if unset) and verifies the signature over the raw received object (401 on mismatch) via the shared rejectInvalidCallback guard, while non-linear sources route to the slack-bot binding for backward compatibility.

A queued message without a callback context has no safe callback destination — completion delivery is intentionally skipped, visible as has_callback_context:false on the control plane's prompt.enqueue log — and the LinearCallbackContext schema is a strict union in which the transitionIssueOnStart:true variant requires organizationId and appUserId.

Start and completion callbacks are delivered with one retry (2 attempts, 1 s apart, 10 s per-attempt timeout) by the shared delivery helper; notifyStarted fires as a background task only when a Linear-source message with callback context is dispatched to the sandbox WebSocket.

POST /callbacks/start moves the issue to its team's started workflow only when the context carries transitionIssueOnStart:true — set only for action "created" webhooks with a human creatorId — and is acknowledged with outcome stale_callback when the signed payload is older than 5 minutes or more than 60 s in the future; Linear calls are bounded by a 20-second abort signal (504 on timeout, 503 on auth failure, 502 on transition failure), and a skipped, rejected, or failed transition never blocks agent execution.

transitionIssueToStarted moves an issue forward to the team's lowest-position started workflow state in one context query plus one issueUpdate, classifying everything else as a no-op (already_started, terminal_completed, terminal_canceled, no_started_state, issue_not_found); follow-ups, automation sessions, and already-progressed issues remain unchanged.

The control plane throttles tool_call callbacks to one per 3 seconds per session and dedupes per tool callId, marking a callId delivered only on success; the worker skips when the context lacks agentSessionId/organizationId/appUserId or when emitToolProgressActivities is explicitly false (defaulting to enabled for contexts that predate the field), formats tools into Linear's action/parameter shape with truncation and non-empty placeholders, and swallows emission failures.

On /callbacks/complete the worker extracts the agent response from control-plane events and artifacts, emits a response (success) or error (failure) terminal activity, updates the agent session's plan to completed/failed, and when a PR artifact exists sets externalUrls to View Session plus Pull Request links; Linear leaves "Working" only after the terminal activity is delivered, and a skipped completion cannot repair itself later — recovery is a new follow-up through the same agent session.

When the completion callback context lacks Agent API identity, the worker falls back to posting an issue comment via the optional LINEAR_API_KEY; without that key configured it logs callback.no_linear_api_key and gives up.

All bot→control-plane calls (session create, prompt, stop, repos, environments, integration settings) are signed sig1 as service "linear-bot" with the worker's own SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET and sent through the CONTROL_PLANE service binding; session-creation and prompt calls assert the actor header linear:{linearUserId}, which the control plane parses as a bot-format author id for identity linking.

The worker's HTTP surface is exactly /health, /oauth/authorize, /oauth/callback, /webhook, and /callbacks/{start,complete,tool_call}; there are no /config/* endpoints in the router — team/project mappings and user preferences are operator-managed KV keys edited with wrangler, and integration settings resolve from the control plane.

The worker's Env requires the LINEAR_KV KV namespace and the CONTROL_PLANE service binding plus the Linear OAuth/webhook secrets; the classifier binds exactly one of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY selected by CLASSIFICATION_MODEL, and LINEAR_API_KEY is an optional legacy fallback.

Terraform deploys the linear-bot worker when enable_linear_bot is true (validation requires non-empty linear_client_id, linear_client_secret, and linear_webhook_secret), wires the LINEAR_KV namespace and the CONTROL_PLANE service binding, attaches the reciprocal LINEAR_BOT service binding to the control-plane worker together with SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET_LINEAR_BOT, and outputs the webhook and OAuth authorize URLs.

Security posture of the Linear path: Linear client credentials, runtime access tokens, webhook secrets, and callback secrets stay server-side; Linear does not provide Git credentials — repository access comes from the deployment's source-control integration such as the GitHub App — and Linear issue titles, descriptions, comments, and agent prompts may be sent to the coding agent, so they must not contain secrets.
